_note: Known disagreements between spec/permission-matrix.yaml and what the code enforces.
scripts/check_permissions.py re-derives this census from live values on every run and
requires an EXACT match in both directions: a new or widened divergence reds, and so
does an entry for a divergence that has been resolved. Fixing one and removing its line
are necessarily the same change. Each divergence entry carries BOTH directions — `extra`
(code grants beyond the matrix) and `refused` (code refuses a role the matrix grants) —
so revoking a matrix-granted role without updating this file reds exactly like a new grant.
This file records reality, not approval. Every entry is an open decision, and each has
exactly two honest resolutions: either the matrix under-declares what the product is
meant to do (widen the matrix), or the code is more permissive than the contract
(narrow the code). Nothing here should be closed by editing whichever side is easier.
All nine divergences run the same direction — the code grants more than the contract —
and no site currently refuses a role the matrix grants. That uniformity is itself
evidence: role sets were written per-module against local need and never checked against
the declared contract, because until now nothing could check.
unnamed_capabilities entries are `key|sorted,members` signatures, not bare keys — a
key-only baseline cannot see a still-unnamed site WIDEN its enforced role set, since the
key does not change when the set does.

contact_roster:AUTHORIZED_CONTACT_ROLES.why: The gate gates DECRYPTION of publicist/manager/agent name, email, phone and notes — it is passed as allowed_roles into the field vault (contact_roster.py:341,523) and gates reveal at api.py:463. The matrix does not grant host `contacts`. If the matrix is right, a host can decrypt third-party contact PII it was never meant to see.
resolutions: widen matrix: host is intended to see contacts
narrow code: remove host from the roster gate

touchpoints:AUTHORIZED_TOUCHPOINT_ROLES.why: Same shape as the roster: encrypted notes on informal guest contact across text/email/ig/in-person/phone/hallway. Matrix does not grant host `touchpoints`.

guest_crm:AUTHORIZED_HISTORY_ROLES.why: Bears directly on finding H-73.9, which wants hosts admitted to guest history in the dashboard. The matrix ALREADY grants host `guest_history`; the divergence is the opposite way — the code additionally admits editorial_owner and producer, whom the matrix does not. H-73.9's client fix is therefore correct and independent of this row.
resolutions: widen matrix to match the working product

clearances:CLEARANCE_DECISION_ROLES.why: Matrix grants decides:clearances to editorial_owner alone; the code also admits producer and relationship_owner. Rights clearance authorizes publication, so this is the widest decision gap of the eight module-level sites.

notifications:TEAM_ROLES.why: Surfaced by wiring this site's proposed capability (`reads:notifications`) into the map instead of leaving it None: the matrix already grants that capability to `editor` alone, but the code admits every team role — editorial_owner, host, network_operator, producer, and relationship_owner — to the notifications feed. This was invisible before because the site's capability field was None, which routed it into `unnamed_sites()` instead of `divergences()`, even though the matrix has named this concept since 1.0.
resolutions: widen matrix: notifications are meant for the whole team, not just editor
narrow code: gate the feed to editor alone

sponsors:WRITE_ROLES.why: Matrix grants decides:sponsor_inventory to producer alone; the code also admits editorial_owner and relationship_owner.

sponsors:CLAIM_APPROVAL_ROLES.why: Matrix grants decides:sponsor_claim_approval to editorial_owner alone; the code also admits relationship_owner.

pilot_service:DECISION_ROLES.why: Matrix grants decides:pilot_runs to relationship_owner alone; the code also admits editorial_owner and producer.

distribution:READ_ROLES.why: A network operator can read the distribution pipeline; the matrix scopes that role to network-level reads and does not list `pipeline`. Most likely genuine matrix under-declaration.

_unnamed.why: Five enforcement points have no matrix vocabulary at all, so the contract cannot govern them even in principle. Each already carries its proposed name as `capability` in hospes/permissions.py (not None) so that adding the name to the matrix activates divergence checking automatically, without a second synchronized code edit — that is exactly what happened to notifications:TEAM_ROLES above, which is why this list is five entries, not six.

_uncovered.why: 39 role sets exist in hospes/*.py; the import-based census can only see the 18 bound to a module-level name that ENFORCEMENT_SITES maps. The other 21 are written inline at a call site, or live inside a table (service._RECEIPT_ROLES maps seven receipt types to seven role sets), and were therefore invisible to the first cut of this gate — which reported '18 enforcement points' as though that were the surface.
_uncovered.why_it_matters: A completeness gate that under-reports is worse than no gate: it retires the question with a green tick. This list makes the gap declared and frozen rather than silent, and the signature carries members, so a site already known to be uncovered still reds if it WIDENS.
_uncovered.shape_of_the_fix: Each entry leaves by being covered, not by being deleted. Inline sets promote to a module-level constant and gain an ENFORCEMENT_SITES row; the _RECEIPT_ROLES table needs a per-receipt capability vocabulary the matrix does not have yet. demo_guide:_KNOWN_ROLES is the one that may legitimately stay — it validates demo personas and enforces nothing — but it is listed rather than special-cased, because an exemption nobody can see is the same defect one level up.
_uncovered.notable: partnership_records:_require_owner_role is an eighth role helper the plan's survey missed entirely — it has a different name from the other seven and gates on an inline literal, so neither a grep for _require_role nor an import-based census finds it.
